clue.text: Sure boat at sea is a destroyer

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters of the two words before it are jumbled

explanation.surface: A boat that is sure to sink things at sea sounds like a warship, a destroyer.
explanation.definitionFit: A saboteur wrecks machinery or plans deliberately, so he is literally one who destroys.

clue.text: Dog Bill's entered into competition

indicators.note: entered into says one piece goes inside another, here the bill goes into the competition

parts.note: a show is a competition, as in a dog show or flower show
a bill is a poster or advertisement, AD for short; the 's is 'is', joining it to its indicator

explanation.surface: A dog called Bill has been entered in a dog show.
explanation.definitionFit: To dog someone is to follow them closely, which is also what to shadow means as a verb.

clue.text: Document holder that won't hold the cops up long?

definitions.text: Document holder that won't hold the cops up long?

parts.words: Document holder that won't hold the cops up long?
parts.note: a case for papers, read as a police case that is brief, one that will not delay the police for long

explanation.surface: A wallet for documents is described as if it were an investigation the police will clear up quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: The plain part is a holder for documents; the question mark flags the second reading, a short (brief) case for the police.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat leather bag for carrying papers to work is exactly a holder for documents.

clue.text: Liberating moment of joyful truth he arranged

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of the words before it are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A moment of joyful truth that someone arranged sounds like a liberating revelation.
explanation.definitionFit: Independence Day in the United States marks the 1776 declaration that freed the colonies from British rule.

clue.text: A little drunk now, number 3 in maths?

indicators.note: A little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone slightly tipsy is asked about the third number in a maths problem.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition left 'number 3' out; the hidden run takes the N of 'number', and '3 in maths?' is the definition: 3-down's last word ends in Y, a letter used for an algebra variable.
explanation.definitionFit: In algebra a letter such as y stands for a quantity not yet known, a variable to be solved for.

clue.text: After endless smooch, satisfied with one's lot!

indicators.note: After says the next piece comes behind the trimmed word for smooch
endless says the word for smooch loses its final letter

parts.note: a smooch is a kiss
to satisfy a need is to meet it, so satisfied is met

explanation.surface: After a long kiss someone feels content with their lot in life.
explanation.definitionFit: Kismet is fate or destiny, the fortune that falls to a person, their lot.

clue.text: "I'll do what I like", it could be said on 3

definitions.meaning: a defiant remark claiming freedom to act as one wishes
3-down is American Independence Day, a day when a nation celebrates its liberty

explanation.surface: A defiant speaker insists on doing as they please on Independence Day.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition refers to the answer at 3-down, the American national holiday celebrating independence.
explanation.definitionFit: People say this phrase to claim the liberty to do as they please, and on Independence Day Americans celebrate their freedom.

clue.text: Tiny little piece, Mozart's final composition

parts.note: a mote is a speck, a tiny particle of dust

indicators.note: final says to take only the last letter of the composer's name

explanation.surface: A short piece of music was the last thing Mozart composed.
explanation.definitionFit: A motet is a short choral work, usually sacred, so it is a musical composition.

clue.text: Two things golfer wants, the first picked up in tin

indicators.note: picked up means heard, and only the first of the two things is changed by sound, giving a drink

parts.note: a golfer needs a tee to rest the ball on and a caddy to carry the clubs

explanation.surface: A golfer wants two things, and the first one gets picked up off the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' looks like lifting the tee off the grass; it is the sound signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea caddy is a small container, often a metal tin, for keeping loose leaves.

clue.text: Oblivious to the right marks in a test

indicators.note: in says the currency piece is placed inside the other words

parts.note: an oral is a spoken examination, a test
M is short for marks, the old German currency

explanation.surface: Someone unaware of the correct answers in an exam.
explanation.definitionFit: An amoral person has no sense of right and wrong, unaware of what is morally correct.

clue.text: Main song line directed at the audience

definitions.meaning: on a single record the A side carries the featured track
in a play, a remark spoken to the audience that other characters are taken not to hear

explanation.surface: A singer's chief number includes a line sung straight out to the crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor's aside is a remark to the audience; a record's A side holds its lead track.

clue.text: In part, USA makes revolutionary guide to good relations

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the hidden letters are read backwards
In part says the letters sit inside the following words

explanation.surface: America is said to have written a revolutionary guide to good international relations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' and 'part' share the clue's opening: the run is inside 'part, USA makes', and 'revolutionary' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Indian text is famous as a manual of lovemaking, a guide to sexual relations.

clue.text: Not in the pink, maybe somewhat blue

definitions.meaning: in the pink means in good health, so this is feeling unwell
blue jokes are rude ones, so somewhat blue is a bit risqué

explanation.surface: Colour words play off each other: not pink, perhaps a little blue.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both slightly ill and slightly indecent, as with a risqué joke.

clue.text: Decree carrying a lot of weight with American

parts.note: someone carrying a lot of weight is fat

explanation.surface: A weighty ruling issued alongside an American one.
explanation.definitionFit: A fatwa is a legal ruling issued by an Islamic scholar, a religious decree.

clue.text: Unproductive member of the nobility, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word for the nobleman is to be taken by its sound

parts.note: a baron is a nobleman of the lowest rank of peer

explanation.surface: An idle aristocrat is said to do nothing useful.
explanation.definitionFit: Barren land or effort yields nothing, so it is fruitless and unproductive.

clue.text: Pull swimmer back in sheltered area

indicators.note: back says the pieces are read in the reverse direction

parts.note: to draw is to pull, as a horse draws a cart
an eel is a fish, a swimmer

explanation.surface: Someone hauls a swimmer back into a sheltered spot out of the waves.
explanation.definitionFit: The lee side is the one sheltered from the wind, so it is the protected side or area.

clue.text: Merchant of Venice gets flipping cool director

parts.note: Antonio is the title merchant in Shakespeare's play

indicators.note: flipping means turned over, so the word for cool is read backwards

parts.note: in means fashionable, cool

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's merchant meets a seriously cool film-maker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' looks like a mild British expletive qualifying cool; it is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Michelangelo Antonioni was an Italian film director, known for Blow-Up.

clue.text: Rubbish bishop with messy hair, mostly

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: mostly says the word loses its last letter

parts.note: messy hair is uncombed

explanation.surface: A dishevelled bishop with untidy hair looks like rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Buncombe, the root of bunkum, means empty talk or nonsense.

clue.text: Passing water duct in old city with churned earth

parts.note: Ur is the ancient city of Mesopotamia

indicators.note: churned means stirred up, so the letters of the next word are mixed

explanation.surface: A water channel in an ancient city runs through churned-up earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passing water' looks like water flowing by; it means urinating.
explanation.definitionFit: The tube through which urine leaves the body is a duct for urinating.

clue.text: Drivers' group fixing vehicle's motor problem

indicators.note: fixing means securing a piece in place, here the vehicle held between the letters of the group

parts.note: the AA, the Automobile Association, is a British motoring organisation offering breakdown help
a taxi is a vehicle; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: The breakdown service is repairing a car with an engine fault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'motor problem' looks like a car fault; it is a medical condition affecting movement.
explanation.definitionFit: Ataxia is loss of muscle coordination, a disorder of the body's motor control.

clue.text: Female writer of a vacuous lyric going too far

indicators.note: vacuous means empty, so the inside of the word is emptied out, leaving its outside letters

parts.note: OTT, over the top, means going too far

explanation.surface: A woman writer's song lyric is both empty and excessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Louisa May Alcott was an American novelist, best known for Little Women.

clue.text: Forage in area by Florida, doubling back

indicators.note: back says the whole string is read in reverse
doubling says the state's abbreviation appears twice

parts.note: FLA is an abbreviation for the US state of Florida

explanation.surface: Someone looks for food in a region of Florida, doubling back on their route.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucerne is a plant grown to feed livestock, fodder for animals.

clue.text: Routine drug overdose

parts.note: meth is short for methamphetamine

explanation.surface: A habitual drug user overdoes it as a matter of course.
explanation.definitionFit: A method is a set procedure, a regular way of doing something, a routine.

clue.text: Waste drink with considerable volume

parts.note: cha is a word for tea
FF, fortissimo, is the music marking for very loud

explanation.surface: Someone throws away a drink, taking a large amount.
explanation.walkthrough: 'volume' looks like quantity of liquid; it is loudness.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaff is the husk left after threshing grain, worthless refuse.

clue.text: Getting jazzy, eager to harmonise

indicators.note: getting jazzy means being livened up or jumbled, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Musicians eager to play jazz try to sing in harmony.
explanation.definitionFit: To agree is to be in accord, the figurative sense of being in harmony.

clue.text: A virus stops criminal having cash to splash

indicators.note: stops means plugs, so the virus fills a gap inside the criminal

parts.note: a fence is a criminal who deals in stolen goods
flu, influenza, is caused by a virus

explanation.surface: A virus halts a crook who has money to throw around.
explanation.definitionFit: Affluence is wealth, the state of being rich enough to spend freely.

clue.text: Bandicoot, say, camouflaged in puma's lair

indicators.note: camouflaged means disguised, so the letters of the following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A small animal hides itself in a big cat's den.
explanation.definitionFit: The bandicoot of Australia carries its young in a pouch, an example of a pouched mammal.

clue.text: It was pledged to be red hot

parts.note: a Trot, a Trotskyist, is a left-winger, a red
H is short for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Someone vowed to be passionate and fiery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'red hot' reads as one phrase; it splits into a communist and a tap marking.
explanation.definitionFit: Troth is a solemn promise, as in plighting one's troth at a wedding.

clue.text: Still keeping extremely lovely 17th- century recorder

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: even, as in 'even more', means still

indicators.note: extremely means take the extreme letters of the next word

explanation.surface: A beautiful old recorder, the instrument, from the 1600s survives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recorder' suggests the woodwind instrument; it is John Evelyn, the 17th-century English diarist.
explanation.definitionFit: John Evelyn kept a famous diary of seventeenth-century English life, a chronicler of his era.

clue.text: Hen possibly a dotty little creature

definitions.meaning: a hen is a female bird, a lady of the bird world
a small spotted beetle, red with black spots

explanation.surface: A chicken is called a bit crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: The spotted beetle bears the name, and a hen is literally a female, or lady, bird.
